title: Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 1 small head cabbage, cut in wedges
1 medium turnip, peeled and cut in chunks
steps: Soak the salt beef in cold water overnight, then drain.
Put the beef in a large pot, cover with fresh water and bring to a boil. Tie the split peas loosely in a pudding bag or cheesecloth and add to the pot. Simmer 2 hours.
Add the turnip and carrots and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage and simmer about 25 minutes more, until everything is tender.
Lift out the pudding bag, mash the peas with the butter and pepper to make pease pudding.
Slice the beef and serve with the vegetables, pease pudding and a little of the pot liquor.
notes: Save the pot liquor for pea soup the next day.

title: Toutons
steps: Pull off pieces of dough the size of an egg and flatten them to about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat the butter and oil in a heavy frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the toutons 3 to 4 minutes a side until golden and cooked through.
Serve hot with molasses or a pat of butter.
notes: Use leftover homemade dough or a store-bought frozen loaf, thawed and risen. Fatback scrunchions are the traditional fat if you have them.

title: Fish and Brewis
steps: The night before, soak the salt cod and the hard bread in separate bowls of cold water. Change the fish water once or twice.
Drain the fish, cover with fresh water and simmer 15 minutes until it flakes. Drain and flake, removing any bones.
Bring the hard bread and its water to a boil, then drain well.
Fry the salt pork until crisp to make scrunchions. Add the onion and cook until soft.
Gently mix the fish and brewis together and serve topped with the scrunchions, onion and some of the fat.
notes: Hard bread (hard tack) is sold in most Newfoundland grocery stores.

title: Cod au Gratin
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a baking dish.
Simmer the cod in a little water for 5 minutes, drain and break into large pieces in the dish.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute. Whisk in the milk and cook until thickened. Season with salt and pepper and stir in 1 cup of the cheese.
Pour the sauce over the fish. Top with the rest of the cheese and the bread crumbs.
Bake 25 minutes until bubbling and golden.

title: Pea Soup and Doughboys
steps: Soak the salt beef in cold water for a few hours, then drain.
Simmer the beef, split peas and water for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then.
Add the onion, carrot and turnip and simmer 30 minutes.
For the doughboys, mix the flour, baking powder and salt, rub in the butter, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough on top of the simmering soup, cover tightly and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.

title: Blueberry Grunt
steps: In a wide pot with a lid, simmer the blueberries, sugar, water and lemon juice for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Rub in the butter and stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the bubbling berries.
Cover tightly and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are cooked through.
Serve warm with cream or ice cream.
notes: Partridgeberries or a mix of berries work too; add a little more sugar for partridgeberries.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir Fry
steps: Cook the rice.
Toss the beef with the cornstarch and 1 tbsp of the soy sauce.
Mix the rest of the soy sauce with the oyster sauce, brown sugar and broth.
Heat half the oil in a large pan over high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the broccoli with a splash of water. Cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss until glossy. Serve over rice.

title: Easy Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, cut in pieces
steps: Cook the rice.
Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and garam masala and stir 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, coconut milk and salt. Simmer 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with the rice.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
steps: Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beef and brown, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the tomatoes, oregano and salt. Simmer gently 30 to 40 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti, drain and toss with the sauce. Serve with parmesan.
notes: Freezes well. Make a double batch.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil, spices and salt on a large sheet pan.
Roast 20 minutes, stirring halfway, until the chicken is cooked.
Squeeze the lime over and serve in warm tortillas with sour cream and salsa.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Whisk the oil, juice of the lemons, garlic, oregano and salt.
Toss the potatoes and chicken in the mixture and spread in a roasting pan, chicken skin side up. Pour the broth around.
Roast 50 minutes until the chicken is golden and the potatoes are tender, basting once.

title: Chickpea Coconut Curry
steps: Cook the rice.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the garlic and curry paste and stir 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk and chickpeas and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Season with the fish sauce and lime juice. Serve over rice.
notes: A cheap meatless meal. Add leftover chicken or shrimp if you have it.

title: Shepherd's Pie
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with the butter and milk.
Heat the oven to 400°F.
Cook the onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the beef and brown it.
Stir in the flour, then the broth and Worcestershire. Simmer 5 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas and corn.
Spread the meat in a baking dish, top with the potatoes and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake 25 minutes until golden.

title: Seafood Chowder
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp. Add the onion and celery and soften 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock and potatoes. Simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the haddock, scallops and shrimp and simmer gently 5 minutes.
Stir in both milks, the butter and pepper and heat through without boiling.
notes: Use whatever seafood is on sale; cod or mussels work well.

title: Moose Stew
steps: Toss the moose in the flour and brown in batches in the oil in a heavy pot.
Add the onion and cook 3 minutes.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and salt. Cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots, turnip and potatoes and simmer 40 minutes more until tender.
notes: Stewing beef works the same way.

title: Molasses Raisin Bread
steps: Stir the yeast into the warm water with 1 tbsp of the molasses and let it foam, about 10 minutes.
Add the rest of the molasses, the butter and salt. Mix in the flour to make a soft dough and knead 8 minutes. Knead in the raisins.
Let rise in a greased bowl until doubled, about 1 1/2 hours.
Shape into a loaf in a greased loaf pan and let rise 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F for 35 to 40 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped.

title: General Tso's Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut in bite-size pieces
steps: Cook the rice.
Toss the chicken with the egg, then with the 1/2 cup cornstarch, flour and salt until well coated.
Heat the frying oil to 350°F in a deep pot. Fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
For extra crunch, fry everything a second time for 1 minute.
Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, vinegar, sugar, broth and 1 tbsp cornstarch together.
In a large pan, heat 1 tbsp oil and fry the garlic, ginger and chilies for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce and stir until thick and glossy.
Toss in the chicken until coated. Top with green onions and serve with rice.
notes: Air fryer option: spray the coated chicken with oil and air fry at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking halfway.

title: General Tso's Chicken (Skillet)
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Cook the rice.
Season the chicken with the garlic salt and paprika, then toss in the flour until every piece is coated.
Heat about 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches, 4 to 5 minutes a side, until golden and cooked through, adding oil as needed. Set aside.
In the same pan, add the soy sauce, hoisin, rice vinegar, brown sugar, broth, garlic, ginger and pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer.
Stir the cornstarch into 2 tbsp cold water, pour into the sauce and cook 2 to 3 minutes until thickened. Stir in the sesame oil.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss until well coated.
Serve over rice, topped with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Chicken thighs make it more tender. Use more or less pepper flakes to taste. Cooking the chicken in batches keeps it crispy. Leftovers reheat well.

title: Newfoundland Molasses Raisin Bread — Overnight Poolish
ingredients: 625 g bread flour, for the poolish
0.5 g instant dry yeast, for the poolish
625 g bread flour, for the final dough
240 g whole milk, lukewarm (up to 365 g if needed)
113 g unsalted butter, melted and cooled
5 g instant dry yeast, for the final dough
steps: DAY 1 – Poolish: Mix the 625 g bread flour, 625 g water (about 20°C) and 0.5 g yeast in a large bowl until no dry flour remains. Cover loosely.
Leave at room temperature (20–21°C) for 12–16 hours. It's ready when it has expanded, is full of bubbles and the surface is just starting to flatten. Don't let it collapse completely.
DAY 2 – Raisins: Rinse the raisins briefly in warm water, drain well and pat dry. Set aside.
Mix: Put all the poolish in the mixing bowl. Add 240 g lukewarm milk, the molasses, beaten eggs, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, cloves and 5 g yeast. Mix briefly until combined.
Add the remaining 625 g flour and mix on low until a rough dough forms. Cover and rest 15–20 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Knead: Add the salt and knead 5–8 minutes until the dough starts to build strength.

Gradually add the melted, cooled butter while kneading. Keep mixing until smooth, elastic and slightly tacky. If it feels too firm, add some of the reserved 125 g milk a little at a time — not all automatically.
Add the drained raisins in the last 1–2 minutes on low speed. The dough should be soft and slightly tacky but hold its shape. Avoid extra flour unless absolutely necessary.

First rise: Put the dough in a lightly buttered bowl, cover and leave at about 23–25°C for 1½–2½ hours, until roughly doubled. Molasses, butter and eggs slow it down, so it may take longer than ordinary bread.
Shape: Turn onto a lightly floured surface and divide into 3 equal pieces. Flatten each gently, roll into a tight loaf and place in 3 greased 9 × 5 inch loaf pans. Cover loosely.
Final proof: Rise at about 23–25°C for 1–2 hours, until the dough is 2–3 cm above the pan rims and springs back slowly when pressed. Go by the look of the dough, not the clock.
Bake: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake on the middle rack 40–45 minutes. Check at 25–30 minutes and cover loosely with foil if the tops brown too fast. Done at 200–205°F (93–96°C) inside.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.
For a soft traditional crust, brush the hot loaves lightly with melted butter and cover loosely with a clean tea towel while they cool. Cool before slicing.
notes:
Serves = loaves (3 large, about 12 slices each).
Poolish: a true 100% hydration poolish holding 50% of the total flour (1,250 g total flour; 625 g water in the poolish).
Milk: start with 240 g because the poolish adds more water than the original recipe; add the rest only if needed.
Yeast: 0.5 g in the poolish plus 5 g in the final dough for reliable rising with the molasses and butter.
Flour: bread flour gives better structure and moisture.

title: NL Tea Buns
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Combine the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Add the raisins and toss so they're well covered in the flour.
Add the cold butter and crumble it into the flour with your hands.
In another bowl, mix the egg, vanilla, milk and lemon juice.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry and mix to a soft dough. Don't over-knead.
Roll out and cut into buns.
Bake at 350°F for about 25 minutes. Enjoy!
notes:
Makes about a dozen buns, depending on the cutter.
Fresh milk works well.

title: Old-Fashioned Beef Barley Soup
steps: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, adding a little oil if needed.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the beef broth, diced tomatoes, Worcestershire sauce, thyme and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 60 to 90 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the pearl barley and simmer another 35 to 45 minutes, until the barley and beef are tender. Add more broth if needed.
Serve warm with crusty bread.
notes: Serves about 6 (my estimate; the post doesn't say).
